title: Zucchini Fritters
description: The chef Jessica Yang Compagnon, 39, thinks often of the fried zucchini sticks she first had at Tom’s Place, a now-closed diner near her hometown of Yorba Linda, Calif. She currently lives in Paris, where she runs the 11th Arrondissement restaurant Le Rigmarole and the bar Folderol alongside her husband, the chef Robert Compagnon, and adapts this recipe depending on the season. When zucchini isn’t at the market, she substitutes potatoes, onions, sweet potatoes or burdock root. Fritters are delicious at any level of browning and thus are a forgiving introduction to shallow frying — which requires minimal oil — at home.
directions: Grate zucchini on the big-hole side of a box grater and then chop the white and light green parts of the scallions. Mix the two together and season with salt, then let the mixture sit for 10 minutes in a colander or mesh strainer. Drain and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Set aside.

To make the sauce, combine mayonnaise, yogurt, garlic, then add 6 to 8 grinds of black pepper, the juice of a quarter of a lemon and 2 splashes of fish sauce. Mix with a whisk and season to taste. Set aside.
To make the fritters, mix the remaining dry ingredients, then add the egg and egg yolk and zucchini/scallion mixture and stir until combined. The batter should be thick enough to hold its shape.

Fill a pan with about ¾ inch of oil and heat on high until shimmering. Form patties with your hands, making them as flat as possible and about 3 inches in diameter. Fry them until they’re golden brown on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and repeat. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and salt before serving with the sauce on the side.
